Hi Olivia — thanks for the questionnaire. Answers below, short & actionable; I attached a one-page PDF (Clearsight_SQ_Responses_v1.pdf) you can drop into your vendor pack. If you want formal attestation language for procurement, loop in Marissa and she can provide an SLA-friendly blurb.

Q1) Where are prompt/response payloads stored by default for the hosted API?
A1) Default: customer request/response payloads are stored in our multi-tenant hosted region that services the shortest-latency endpoint (US-West by default for US customers). We maintain logical tenancy per customer (metadata and routing), and payloads are stored in encrypted object stores and short-term KV caches on GPUs.

Q2) What are the default retention windows for transient (cache) vs persisted logs?
A2) Default retention (hosted):
  - GPU runtime caches (prefix/KV cache): ephemeral, cleared after 24 hours of inactivity; cache entries are treated as transient and not included in analytics exports.
  - Short-term request/response buffer (for streaming reliability): retained up to 48 hours to allow safe session recovery.
  - Audit and usage logs (tokens, timestamps, routing decisions): retained 90 days by default for billing and troubleshooting.
  - Aggregated metrics and long-term analytics (no PII/payloads): retained for 13 months.

Q3) If we request erasure for a tenant, what is the timeline and mechanism for purge across live, cache, and backup copies?
A3) Erasure flow (hosted API):
  - Step 1 — Initiation: customer files request via privacy@redwood.ai or the Console erasure workflow. We issue a ticket and estimated schedule within 24 hours.
  - Step 2 — Live store purge: immediate removal of tenant data from primary object store and KV indexes; confirmed within 6 hours.
  - Step 3 — Tombstone & background scrub: we mark associated records and begin scrubbing dependent indices and caches. Caches are invalidated immediately; residual cache garbage is cleaned within 7 days.
  - Step 4 — Backups/snapshots: incremental backups and daily snapshots are immutable for a limited window. Backups are cryptographically shredded to remove keys referencing the tenant within 45 days; complete removal from all backup media is completed within 90 days in the normal course. For expedited erasure (contracted enterprise option) we can prioritize snapshot re-write, typically reducing the window to 30–45 days.
  - Step 5 — Confirmation: we provide a signed erasure certificate and artifact list when the process completes.

Q4) Do you offer region-locking for hosted customers or require Dedicated for strict data locality?
A4) Hosted offering: we provide regional pinning to restrict where requests are routed (US, EU, APAC) for customers on our Business tier and above. Region-locking is enforced at routing, storage, and logging layers; however, for absolute physical isolation and dedicated tenancy (e.g., single-tenant hardware) we recommend Redwood Dedicated/Private. We can hybridize a hosted regional pin with contractual data residency terms for Clearsight as part of procurement.

Q5) Are system backups or snapshots encrypted and how long are they retained?
A5) Backups & encryption:
  - All backups and snapshots are encrypted at rest with customer-segregated KMS keys for enterprise accounts; for standard hosted customers we use our managed KMS with SSAE-ready controls.
  - Retention: automated daily snapshots retained for 90 days; point-in-time restore windows align with that 90-day retention. Long-term disaster recovery archives (if configured) are held up to 365 days and stored encrypted.

Attachments included: Clearsight_SQ_Responses_v1.pdf (one page, Q+A + timeline).

If you want any specific redlines for contract language (e.g., shrink backup window from 90 to 30 days), Marissa is the best person to help and we can include addenda to the MSAs.

Thanks,
Ben
